brief_summary: Triple combination of metformin, DPP4 inhibitor and Thiazolidinedione would be a good option in the treatment of drug-naïve Korean type 2 diabetic patients. Newly developed thiazolidinedione, Lobeglitazone would be not inferior to Pioglitazone.
brief_title: Comparison of Lobeglitazone With Pioglitazone as Initial Triple Therapy for Diabetes Management

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* HbA1c \> 13.0 %
* No treatment with insulin or oral agents for 6 months
* 20 ≤ Age \< 80 years

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contraindication to sitagliptin or metformin or thiazolidinedione
* Pregnant or breast feeding women
* Type 1 diabetes, gestational diabetes, or secondary forms of diabetes
* Not appropriate for oral antidiabetic agent
* Medication which affect glycemic control
* Disease which affect efficacy and safety of drugs
* Any major illness (Liver disease, Renal failure, Heart disease, Cancer, etc)

official_title: Comparison of Therapeutic Efficacy Between Lobeglitazone and Pioglitazone as Initial Triple Therapy With Metformin and Sitagliptin in Drug-naïve Type 2 Diabetic Patients
